transcript.text: From what you have described, the most likely cause is blower fan / impeller. Can you hear/feel the fan moving air, and is it clear of fluff?
No sound at all when I press start, so can't hear any fan. Lights come on though. The door has felt loose for a few days and doesn't seem to click shut.

From what you have described, the most likely cause is door handle / catch (mechanical). With the dryer unplugged, look at the catch on the door and the slot it clicks into: fluff or a bit of fabric can stop it engaging, and check the door lines up when you close it. Is the catch broken, was something stopping it (now cleared), or does it all look fine?
Yes it's broken - the plastic tongue on the door has snapped off, found the piece on the floor. If I hold the door shut and press start it runs, stops when I let go.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle / catch (mechanical)]
From what you have found, this points to the door handle / catch (mechanical). To find the right part, could you give me the make and model number? It is usually on a sticker inside the door opening.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Hotpoint. I don't know the model number offhand, I'll go and look inside the door recess now.

[Heading: Likely cause: door handle]
The checks point to the door handle. If the model number can't be read, it is often also on the guarantee card, the receipt or the manual; with it, the right part can be matched. Without it, an appliance engineer can identify and fit the right door handle from the machine itself.
